thread.title: Why Apple still wanted to use Qualcomm’s modems in its latest generation of iPhones

author: James Conlon
title: Why Apple still wanted to use Qualcomm’s modems in its latest generation of iPhones
text:
January 15, 2019 Why Apple still wanted to use Qualcomm’s modems in its latest generation of iPhones
Qualcomm and Apple’s ongoing legal fights have been among some the most interesting one within the tech space. The conflict has now further expanded into an antitrust filing, done by the United States Federal Trade Commission against the Qualcomm, which is now an undergoing trial.
From the most recent testimony, revealed in the case was the admission by Apple Inc’s Chief Operating Officer, Jeff Williams, that in spite of their disputes, Apple Inc (AAPL) still wanted to use Qualcomm (QCOM)’s modems in its latest generation of iPhones. The newest iPhones exhibiting poorer connectivity, than the previous generation its not a hidden fact, that’s why, Apple still wanted to use Qualcomm’s modems.
Qualcomm had previously paid Apple Inc as much as $1 billion, in order to secure the Cupertino giant’s business, so it is quite the departure for the chip-maker to give up what would have been a very lucrative source of income for the company.
Qualcomm refused to do so, Williams suggested, because of the many legal battles between the two companies are fighting all over the world. Since the Federal Trade Commission (FTC)’s contention in its own filing against Qualcomm is that the chip-maker employed anti-competitive practices to prevent others from supplying Apple Inc, it may be interesting to see what effect, if any, Qualcomm’s voluntary refusal to supply modems for the iPhone Xs and Xr will have on the agency’s case.
